article.Citation/Title: Kurland, A. A., Unger, S., Shaffer, J. W., & Savage, C. (1967). Psychedelic therapy utilizing LSD in the treatment of the alcoholic patient: A preliminary report. American Journal of Psychiatry, 123(10), 1202-1209.
article.SourcePDF: alcohol/Kurland, A. A., Unger, S., Shaffer, J. W., & Savage, C. (1967). Psychedelic therapy utilizing LSD in the treatment of the alcoholic patient_ a pre.pdf
article.Outcome: 23/69 (33%) abstinent at 6-month follow-up (single-arm pre/post rate, no comparator)
article.InterventionDescription: LSD 450 mcg, single high-dose session (~10-12 hrs) with eyeshades and stereo music, embedded in ~3 weeks (12-15 hrs) individual psychotherapy; inpatient hospital setting.

article.Outcome: The paper's narrative emphasis (abstract, MMPI figures 1-5) is mental-health change, but the MMPI results are only ever reported as 'all... statistically significant' with no values, N, or test statistics printed anywhere, so they cannot supply a quantitative Outcome. The only fully quantified, SUD-related result in the article is in the Conclusion: 'only 23 patients, or exactly one-third, had maintained abstinence up to the six-month follow-up' (23/69 = 33%). This is a single-arm pre/post rate with no comparator; selected per the SUD-behavioral precedence rule as the sole outcome carrying a usable number, consistent with the task instruction that a no-comparator study yields a single-arm-rate Outcome.
article.SD: No dispersion or test statistic accompanies the 23/69 abstinence figure anywhere in the text. The MMPI section states clinical-scale changes are 'statistically significant' but never prints a test name, statistic, df, or SD, so SD is coded '.' for the chosen Outcome.
article.PVal: No p-value is given for the abstinence rate. The MMPI section asserts significance ('all are statistically significant') but prints no p-value or threshold anywhere in the article, so PVal is coded '.' for the chosen Outcome.
article.SampleSize_NFinal: 69 is the full pilot cohort ('69 male inpatients were treated as described'; 'in the 69 cases under discussion'), and the abstinence fraction is explicitly computed over this same cohort ('23 patients, or exactly one-third' = 23/69), so 69 is used as the denominator for Outcome. The article does not separately report how many of the 69 were actually reachable/assessed at 6 months, so this denominator assumes the stated fraction applies to the full enrolled cohort.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: Objective, setting, intervention detail, outcomes measured, results, harms, and funding source are all explicitly described. Not described: formal inclusion/exclusion criteria (only 'male inpatients' is given), any statistical methods or test names, sample-size/power justification, and no explicit statement that the study was non-randomized/unblinded/uncontrolled (the contrast with 'a controlled study' initiated later implies it, but nothing states directly that this cohort had no randomization, blinding, or comparator). n_met=8 of 14, below the 13-of-14 threshold, so MethodologyDescribedYN=0.

article.Pos Result Y/N: Single-arm study; judged on the study's own pre/post direction per the boundary rule. MMPI clinical-scale changes were reported as significant and in a positive direction (except Hypomania), and the authors' own framing ('psychedelic therapy does add significantly to presently available alcoholic rehabilitation resources'; 'the extent of benefit in some cases has seemed considerable') and the 33% abstinence figure support a positive-direction verdict (1), not a null/negative one.
article.RandomizationYN / BlindingYN / Double+Bl: Single-arm, open-label pilot: all 69 patients received the same one-session LSD procedure with no control or comparison group, no randomization, and no blinding described anywhere. Per the v1.2 single-arm boundary rule these are coded 0 (absent design elements), not 3.
article.Clincial Trial YN: Coded 1 to match the eligibility screen: a prospectively planned intervention (structured LSD session within a defined ~3-week psychotherapy course) administered to a defined enrolled cohort (69 male inpatients) for research purposes, with prospective outcome assessment (MMPI, EEG, cognitive testing, 6-month abstinence follow-up). Single-arm/open-label does not disqualify it as a trial.
article.Retention (%): Not calculable. The article gives only the numerator/denominator for abstinence (23/69) at 6 months; it never separately reports how many of the 69 enrolled/treated patients were retained in follow-up versus lost to follow-up, so no completers/denominator arithmetic is possible. Coded '.'.
article.InclusionExclusionCriteria: Only a minimal population description is given ('69 male inpatients' hospitalized in the Alcoholic Rehabilitation Unit); no explicit inclusion or exclusion criteria (diagnostic threshold, age range, psychiatric or medical exclusions) are stated, so coded 0 per the project's strict not-reported-is-not-met convention.
article.ConfoundYN: No statistical adjustment, stratification, or substantive discussion of confounding/moderating/mediating factors appears anywhere in the article. Coded 0.
article.Power: No a priori or post hoc power discussion, or any statement of the study being under/over-powered, appears anywhere. Coded 0.
article.PrimaryCare: Treatment was delivered entirely within a state psychiatric hospital's specialized Alcoholic Rehabilitation Unit and its own outpatient follow-up team; no primary-care setting or provider interface is described. Coded 0.
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: Patients are described only as 'hospitalized in the Alcoholic Rehabilitation Unit' with no stated recruitment method (consecutive admissions vs. selective volunteer enrollment, screening steps). Because this is a real hospital inpatient population it is plausibly representative, but since the recruitment method itself is never described, coded 0 per the project's strict not-reported-is-not-met convention.
article.BaseStatus: Coded 'Severe' based on multiple convergent textual anchors: the sample is chronic, hospitalized alcoholics ('the prodromal phase... average of ten to 12 years of heavy to excessive drinking'; one illustrative patient 'continuously intoxicated for nearly 18 months'), and the discussant explicitly characterizes the population as having 'chronic and severe alcoholism'.
article.Age_Median: No age data (mean, median, or range) for the 69-patient sample is reported anywhere in the text. Coded '.'.
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: No race/ethnicity data for the sample is reported. Coded '.'.
article.SocioeconomicStatusYN: One illustrative individual case (Figure 5 patient) is described as 'an unskilled laborer, intellectually dull, poorly educated, and culturally deprived,' but this is a single case vignette, not a description of SES for the sample as a whole or an inclusion criterion. Coded 0.
article.Implementation Outcome: The text notes anecdotally that 'the introduction of this procedure met with rapid and lasting patient, staff, and administrative acceptance,' but this is a narrative aside, not a measured feasibility/acceptability/fidelity outcome with any instrument or systematic assessment. Coded 0.
article.AnyAEReported: SafetyReported=Y because the authors explicitly assessed safety (independent EEG ratings pre/post in 20 consecutive patients, a battery of intellectual-functioning tests, ongoing clinical evaluation) and state a direct conclusion: 'no patient has been harmed.' The Treatment Procedure section mentions the therapist 'aborting anxiety or other turbulent or disruptive episodes' and reviewing possible reactions (fear, depression, paranoia, confusion) with patients beforehand, but this is generic description of the therapist's standing role/preparatory counseling, not a reported incidence of any specific AE with a count or named case in this cohort. Given the article's explicit 'no patient has been harmed' claim and the absence of any counted or named adverse event, this is coded as the 'no AEs occurred' case: AnyAEReported=N, NumDistinctAEs=0, WorstSeverity=None, ae_events=[].
article.InterventionDescription: Source text prints the LSD dose as '450 pg.' — almost certainly an OCR/ligature misread of '450 μg' (micrograms), consistent with the well-documented Spring Grove/Kurland program's standard 300-450 mcg LSD dosing. The number 450 itself is unambiguous; only the unit abbreviation is a legibility artifact, so it is read through per the ligature-artifact allowance and written as '450 mcg'.
article.EligibleYN: Both criteria met. (a) Clinical trial: a prospectively planned intervention (structured ~3-week psychotherapy course incorporating one high-dose LSD session) delivered to a defined enrolled cohort (69 male inpatients) for research purposes, with prospective outcome assessment (MMPI, EEG, cognitive testing, 6-month follow-up) — single-arm/open-label per the boundary rule does not disqualify it. (b) SUD outcome: the article reports a substance-use endpoint, six-month abstinence (23/69 maintained abstinence).

config_proposal.note: Single-arm open-label pilot (N=69) with no control or comparison group; the only quantified SUD outcome is a pre/post proportion (23/69, 33% abstinent at 6 months). A single-arm rate has no defensible conversion under any of the seven supported Tier-1 methods (d, g, eta_p, F, chi2, OR, RR), so this is routed to Tier 2 rather than presented as a treatment effect.
config_proposal.tier2_basis: 23/69 (33%) maintained abstinence at 6-month follow-up in a single-arm, open-label pilot; MMPI clinical-scale changes reported as significant and in a positive direction; authors state 'no patient has been harmed' and describe benefit as 'considerable' in some cases.
